issues.legal_issue: Parliament has legislative competence to enact a law governing the interest charged by banking companies.
material_facts: A bank sued to recover money lent to a borrower, and the dispute over interest reached the High Court in a second appeal.

The High Court declared the provision barring courts from reopening bank transactions because interest was excessive to be invalid, reasoning that relief from agricultural indebtedness belonged to the States.
issues.conclusion: The provision was validly enacted under Parliament’s power to legislate with respect to banking.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21-A of the Banking Regulation Act concerns the rate of interest charged by banking companies and falls within Entry 45 of List I of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution. The High Court’s reliance on Entry 30 of List II was misplaced. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.bank_loan_recovery_dispute: A dispute arose in proceedings to recover money lent by a bank.
predicates.law_governs_interest_charged_by_banks: The challenged law regulates interest charged by banking companies.

issues.definition: When a bank recovery dispute concerns a law regulating interest charged by banks, the output is that the law falls within national banking power.

issues.legal_issue: The restriction on reopening bank transactions because interest is excessive applies to loans made by banking companies to both agriculturists and non-agriculturists.
material_facts: The borrower disputed the interest charged on a bank loan.
The High Court relied on the constitutional allocation of agricultural debt relief to the States when declaring the restriction invalid.
issues.conclusion: The provision applies to all types of loans granted by a banking company, whether the borrower is an agriculturist or a non-agriculturist.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21-A of the Banking Regulation Act provides that a transaction between a banking company and its debtor cannot be reopened by a court on the ground that the charged interest rate is excessive. The provision applies to all such loans; Entry 30 of List II does not change its scope. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.loan_granted_by_banking_company: A banking company granted the loan to its borrower.
predicates.court_considers_excessive_interest: A court is asked to reopen the transaction on the ground that its interest rate is excessive.

issues.definition: When a banking company granted a loan and a court is asked to reopen it because its interest rate is excessive, the output is that the transaction cannot be reopened on that ground.

issues.legal_issue: A court may not reduce compound interest agreed to under a mortgage loan merely because the loan is secured by property.
material_facts: The High Court stated that compound interest would normally be excessive when the borrower provided adequate security by mortgaging property.
The dispute concerned interest charged on a bank loan, and the Court treated the mortgage as security for the loan rather than as a basis for changing the agreed interest.
issues.conclusion: If the parties agreed to compound interest on a loan secured by a mortgage, the court cannot interfere to reduce the agreed interest merely because property was mortgaged.
issues.legal_principle: Section 21-A of the Banking Regulation Act bars reopening a banking transaction on the ground that the interest charged is excessive. The Court also applied the principle that a mortgage is a matter of contract and secures repayment; the security has no relation to the quantum of interest agreed. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.compound_interest_agreed: The lender and borrower agreed that compound interest would be paid on the loan.

issues.definition: When a bank loan carries agreed compound interest and property is mortgaged as security, the output is that the agreed interest may not be reduced merely because of that security.
